    clients/game/bin/src/overture/sky.rs:514
    overture::sky::tests::the_sky_is_complete_at_the_very_first_rung
    "figure-count caption missing or wrong: ...The sky holds 4 figures."

    assert!(early_text.contains("The sky holds 2 figures."))   <- expects 2, gets 4

THE ONE BEHIND IT. Four lines further down, in the SAME test:

    assert!(
        early_text.contains("At least one figure stands on the sun's road."),
        "ecliptic caption missing: {early_text:?}"
    );

Your own census says, for seed 42:

    figure-count            = 4     (the test expects 2)
    ecliptic-figure-count   = 0     (the test expects at least 1)
    largest-figure-members  = 6

So seed 42 now has FOUR figures and NONE of them on the ecliptic. Fix the first
assertion and the second fails on the next run.

WHY --no-fail-fast DID NOT SAVE YOU HERE, which is worth knowing generally: the
flag makes the chamber report every failing TEST. Within a single test, the
first failing `assert!` still aborts the function, so assertions two and three
never executed. That limit is inherent to libtest, not something the flag
can reach.

AND THE COMMENT ABOVE THEM IS NOW FALSE IN TWO PLACES. It reads: "Seed 42's
astronomy commits no pole star ... 2 wanderers, 2 figures, and at least one
figure on the ecliptic". Wanderers and the pole star are still right —
`ecliptic-figure-count = 0` means the fourth assertion (no "celestial pole"
caption) is unaffected. But "2 figures" and "at least one figure on the
ecliptic" are both now wrong, and that comment is doing real work: it records
what was VERIFIED, which is why the test reads as a pin on reality rather than
on itself.

WHAT I WOULD DO: update both assertions and the comment in one edit, and say in
the comment that the ecliptic count went to zero under this campaign — that is
a fact about your constellations, not a fixture detail. If the ecliptic caption
should still appear when the count is zero, that is a renderer question and a
different bug; check which before deleting the assertion.

Everything else is clean: gate 6225/6225, both calibration pins re-pinned with
their distinguishing comments, and your yellow row now names the +10.1% CPU
high and separates it from the in-band ratio. This is the last thing I can see.
